components.title: Model endpoints
components.description: Configured local and remote model providers.

implemented-requirements.description: Configured private endpoints are checked before confidential requests are sent.

statements.description: The extension checks a configured private endpoint's connection binding before it sends Confidential content. A mismatch refuses the request instead of falling back to an unpinned connection.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects providers and decides whether their service assurances are sufficient.

implemented-requirements.description: The crypto inventory records listed algorithms and separately records X25519 and scrypt use.

statements.description: The crypto inventory records the listed algorithms used by the product and the collector reports their documented standing.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and approves cryptographic use in its deployment.

statements.description: The inventory records X25519 and scrypt separately, so an unfavorable standing prevents this component from presenting complete cryptographic coverage.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides whether algorithms outside the referenced list are acceptable.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the model endpoints from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-13): what the extension enforces toward them.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension's route check controls what crosses the boundary to a model endpoint before a request is sent.

statements.description: The extension controls what crosses the boundary to model endpoints. Before a request is sent, the route check judges the content's label against the place the request is going to. When your organization's signed rules list places, content above what any cloud may receive goes only to a listed place: a host the list does not name is refused, and content above a listed place's ceiling is refused before it is sent. A listed place reached over https refuses a plain http connection at every level, and a remote endpoint over plain HTTP is refused. Content that any cloud may receive is not limited to the listed places. CI tests of the route check prove these refusals. What a provider does with a request once it arrives is the provider's.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses and approves the model endpoints, lists them in its signed rules with their ceilings, and runs the network boundary of its own sites.

implemented-requirements.description: The extension talks to remote model endpoints only over HTTPS; plain HTTP is allowed only to this computer.

statements.description: The extension sends requests and the API key to remote model endpoints only over HTTPS. A remote endpoint configured over plain HTTP is refused, the API key is never sent to one, and a place your organization's rules list over https refuses a plain http connection at every level. Plain HTTP is allowed only for a runtime on this computer. CI tests of the client, the configuration check and the route check prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the TLS of the model servers it operates, and chooses providers whose endpoints use it.

implemented-requirements.description: Protected B to your organization's own model server goes only over a connection that matches the place's TLS pins.

statements.description: Protected B content to a model server your organization runs goes only through a connection pinned to that place's TLS pins, never the plain fetch. A connection that matches none of the pins is refused, nothing is sent, and the refusal is recorded. CI tests of the route guard prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization issues and rotates the certificates of the servers it runs, and updates the pins in its signed rules.
